title: DeepSpeed Inference: Enabling Efficient Inference of Transformer Models at Unprecedented Scale
technique: Optimized fused transformer kernels for small batch, multi-GPU TP/PP/expert parallelism incl. MoE, and ZeRO-Inference CPU/NVMe offload

optimized_metrics.evidence: a multi-GPU inference solution to minimize latency while maximizing the throughput of both dense and sparse transformer models when they fit in aggregate GPU memory

a heterogeneous inference solution that leverages CPU and NVMe memory in addition to the GPU memory and compute to enable high inference throughput with large models which do not fit in aggregate GPU memory
Meeting the latency requirements of a transformer model inference therefore is equivalent to achieving adequate overall memory bandwidth. Maximizing effective memory bandwidth at small batch sizes

a heterogeneous inference solution that leverages CPU and NVMe memory in addition to the GPU memory and compute to enable high inference throughput with large models which do not fit in aggregate GPU memory

headline_claim.text: DeepSpeed Inference reduces latency by up to 7.3× over the state-of-the-art for latency oriented scenarios and increases throughput by over 1.5x for throughput oriented scenarios. Moreover, it enables trillion parameter scale inference under real-time latency constraints by leveraging hundreds of GPUs

reported_metrics.where: Figs 6-9: latency of generating 8 tokens from 128-token prompt for dense models (batch sweep); MoE per-token latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: (i) latency, i.e., end-to-end output generation time for a batch of input prompts, (ii) token throughput, i.e., tokens-per-second processed, and (iii) compute throughput, i.e., TFLOPS per GPU.
metric_definitions.notes: Latency is batch-level end-to-end generation time for a fixed number of generated tokens (8 for dense, 50 for throughput tests); no request arrivals or queueing. Token throughput counts 'tokens processed' (ambiguous whether prompt tokens included)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For the sparse MoE model, we measure the per-token latency by generating 100 tokens at a time with a prompt of 128 tokens and batch size 8.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-token latency averaged over 100 generated tokens

load_regime: fixed batch size (sweep) at fixed prompt/generation lengths; offline batch for throughput scenarios
tradeoff_acknowledged: Pipeline micro-batch count: 'A small micro-batch count reduces the latency of token-generation but prolongs the latency of prompt processing' (paper discusses a hybrid schedule); latency vs throughput governed by batch size.
